question: A 35-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 3-month history of facial hair growth, acne, and irregular menses. Her friends have told her that her voice sounds lower than usual. Physical examination shows pustular acne and dark hair growth along the jawline. Serum studies show elevated testosterone levels and normal inhibin levels. An ultrasound of the pelvis shows a left-sided ovarian mass. Microscopic examination of the resected ovarian mass shows pale, testosterone-positive staining cells with cytoplasmic Reinke crystal inclusions. These abnormal cells are homologous to which of the following physiological cell type in females?
analysis: The patient's presentation with hirsutism, acne, irregular menses, and elevated testosterone levels along with the presence of a testosterone-positive ovarian mass with Reinke crystal inclusions is indicative of an androgen-secreting tumor. The cells described in the ovarian mass with Reinke crystal inclusions are homologous to Leydig cells in males. In females, the counterpart of Leydig cells are the Theca interna cells.
